curation.lead:
Mark R. Paoletta is a Washington attorney who has served as General Counsel of the Office of Management and Budget under both Trump administrations (January 2018 to January 2021 and January 2025 to present), with concurrent designations as Acting Chief Legal Officer of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and Administrator of the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs in 2025 [Finding #11179][Finding #11191]. His thirty-five-year career has moved through the George H.W. Bush White House Counsel's Office, the House Energy and Commerce Committee's Oversight and Investigations subcommittee (Chief Counsel for Oversight, September 1997 to January 2007), Dickstein Shapiro, DLA Piper, the Office of the Vice President under Mike Pence, OMB under Trump I, and the Washington litigation boutique Schaerr Jaffe LLP (March 26, 2021 to January 2025) [Finding #11179]. The original record of a Williams and Connolly tenure (1992 to 2001) is not supported by the documented timeline.

Concurrent with his Schaerr Jaffe partnership, Paoletta held a Senior Fellow position at the Center for Renewing America, the policy organization founded by Russell Vought, and was named to the advisory board of Project 2025 [Finding #11186]. The December 9, 2024 announcement of his return to OMB explicitly cited both that fellowship and his prior Trump-I tenure with then-OMB Director Vought [Finding #11186][Finding #6688]. Leonard Leo's Judicial Education Project paid Paoletta and MP Strategies LLC approximately $300,000 in 2016 for media work supporting Justice Clarence Thomas, including a documentary, websites, and search-engine optimization [Finding #6681][Finding #7056]. Paoletta is publicly described as a close friend of Leo and prepared Justices Gorsuch, Kavanaugh, and Thomas for their Senate confirmation hearings; he co-edited Created Equal: Clarence Thomas in His Own Words (Regnery, 2022) with Michael Pack [Finding #11193].

As OMB General Counsel during the first Trump administration, Paoletta authored the legal defense of the 2019 Ukraine aid withholding that the Government Accountability Office concluded violated the Impoundment Control Act of 1974 [Finding #6686]. In Trump II he authored a January 27, 2025 OMB memorandum (M-25-13) directing federal agencies to pause all financial assistance, which a federal district court enjoined and OMB rescinded within forty-eight hours, and a separate memorandum asserting that the impoundment power is one of the executive powers vested in the president alone by Article II [Finding #11187][Finding #6688]. As CFPB Acting Chief Legal Officer he issued an April 16, 2025 priority-shift memorandum redirecting consumer-protection enforcement to the states and signed an April 18, 2025 declaration in support of a reduction in force whose accuracy Judge Amy Berman Jackson questioned in the District Court for the District of Columbia [Finding #11191]. Cross-reference of corporate-registry, lobbying, FEC, and court records indicates Paoletta operates as a single legal-architect node connecting the Center for Renewing America, OMB, the Thomas household, Leonard Leo's judicial pipeline, and Schaerr Jaffe [Finding #11201].

sections.title: Career Arc and Institutional Affiliations
sections.content:
Paoletta's career path runs from the George H.W. Bush White House Counsel's Office (Assistant Counsel) to the House Energy and Commerce Committee's Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations, where he served as Chief Counsel for Oversight from September 1997 to January 2007 [Finding #11179]. He moved into private practice in January 2007 as a partner at Dickstein Shapiro, where he led the Congressional Investigations practice, and subsequently joined DLA Piper as a partner in Federal Law and Policy [Finding #11179]. He served as Counsel to Vice President Mike Pence from January 2017 to January 2018 before being appointed General Counsel of the Office of Management and Budget on January 8, 2018, a position he held through January 20, 2021 [Finding #11179][Finding #6679].

On March 26, 2021 Paoletta joined Schaerr Jaffe LLP as a partner, the firm announcing the hire on its website [Finding #11179]. Schaerr Jaffe is a Washington litigation boutique with a roster of seven named partners (Gene Schaerr, Erik S. Jaffe, H. Christopher Bartolomucci, Donald M. Falk, Jeffrey W. Munk, Brian J. Field, Edward H. Trent, and Paoletta) and approximately twenty-five total attorneys; published representative clients include Hobby Lobby, the United States Conference of Catholic Bishops, EWTN, Bayer A.G., AT&T, Fox Corporation, Cato Institute, the US Chamber of Commerce, the Republic of Ecuador, and the US Virgin Islands, with founding partner Gene Schaerr having argued seven Supreme Court cases [Finding #11197]. The firm filed an amicus brief on behalf of Edwin Meese III in Trump v. United States, No. 23-939, on March 19, 2024 [Finding #11197]. Concurrent with his Schaerr Jaffe partnership, Paoletta held a Senior Fellow position at the Center for Renewing America, the organization founded by Russell Vought and designated as an official Project 2025 advisory group; the December 9, 2024 Trump appointment announcement cited that fellowship and his Trump-I tenure with then-OMB Director Vought [Finding #11186]. He returned to OMB as General Counsel on January 20, 2025, and was concurrently designated Acting Chief Legal Officer of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau in 2025 and Administrator of the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs in December 2025 [Finding #11179]. He is also president of MP Strategies LLC and a director of Unreported Story Society (EIN 82-3412341), a 501(c)(3) conservative-media nonprofit [Finding #6679][Finding #7071]. Records do not support the previously reported tenure at Williams and Connolly between 1992 and 2001 [Finding #11179].

sections.title: Judicial Confirmation Work and the Thomas Household
sections.content:
Paoletta's connection to Leonard Leo's judicial-confirmation network is documented across three reinforcing primary records [Finding #11193]. He is publicly described in Project 2025 administration profiles as a close friend of Leo, he prepared Justices Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh, and Clarence Thomas for their Senate confirmation hearings, and he co-edited Created Equal: Clarence Thomas in His Own Words (Regnery, 2022) with Michael Pack, based on twenty-five hours of 2018 to 2019 interviews [Finding #11193]. He maintains the justicethomas.com and anitahillcase.com domains [Finding #11193]. According to Wave-1 systemic-analysis records, his personal friendship with Justice Thomas dates to the 1991 confirmation, during which Paoletta worked in the Bush White House Counsel's Office, and records indicate he was present on the 2019 Crow-funded Indonesia trip with Justice Thomas and Leo [Finding #6692][Finding #6679].

Leonard Leo's Judicial Education Project paid Paoletta and MP Strategies LLC approximately $300,000 in 2016 for what was described as media work supporting Justice Thomas, including a documentary and search-engine optimization [Finding #6681][Finding #7056]. According to reporting cited by the Revolving Door Project and contemporaneous court coverage, Leo arranged $80,000 to $100,000 in consulting payments to Ginni Thomas in 2011 to 2012, routed through Kellyanne Conway's polling firm to the Judicial Education Project and onward to Liberty Consulting [Finding #7075]. Paoletta later served as legal counsel to Virginia "Ginni" Thomas before the House Select Committee to Investigate the January 6th Attack on the United States Capitol; he sent a June 2022 letter resisting the committee's request and managed her voluntary in-person interview, lasting approximately three and a half to four and a half hours, on September 28 to 29, 2022 [Finding #11182][Finding #6684][Finding #7062]. Cross-reference of these records establishes a direct legal nexus between Paoletta and the Thomas household that overlaps with both his MP Strategies consulting income and his subsequent OMB tenure.

sections.title: OMB Executive-Power and Impoundment Architecture
sections.content:
As OMB General Counsel during the first Trump term, Paoletta authored the legal defense of the July 25, 2019 hold on Department of Defense disbursements of Congress-appropriated Ukraine military aid, framing the action as a "programmatic delay" rather than an impoundment [Finding #6686]. The Government Accountability Office concluded on January 16, 2020 that OMB had violated the Impoundment Control Act of 1974 [Finding #6686]. Senator Chris Van Hollen wrote Paoletta on March 12, 2020 demanding his recusal from the GAO inquiry and resignation as OMB Designated Ethics Official [Finding #7064]. On January 19, 2021, the day before the Trump-I administration ended, Paoletta and Vought co-authored a fourteen-page letter to the House Budget Committee laying out their impoundment theory [Finding #7066].

Between administrations, Paoletta and Vought continued to develop the doctrine through the Center for Renewing America, with Paoletta testifying before the House Budget Committee on the Impoundment Control Act, according to the Schaerr Jaffe announcement of his hire [Finding #11187]. In Trump II Paoletta authored two foundational executive-power documents: a memorandum asserting that "the power of impoundment is one such executive power vested in the President alone by Article II," and OMB Memorandum M-25-13 dated January 27, 2025 directing agencies to "temporarily pause all activities related to obligation or disbursement of all federal financial assistance" [Finding #11187][Finding #7052]. The funding-pause memo took effect at 5 p.m. on January 28, 2025; the US District Court for the District of Columbia enjoined it, and OMB issued M-25-14 rescinding it on January 29 [Finding #6688]. According to the Trump appointment statement of December 10, 2024, Paoletta's OMB role was tied to coordination with the Department of Government Efficiency team, with the announcement stating he would "work closely with the DOGE team to cut the size of the bloated Government bureaucracy"; analysis of subsequent OMB output indicates the legal-architect role for DOGE coordination is a continuing one [Finding #6688][Finding #7129].

sections.title: CFPB and Concurrent Agency Restructuring
sections.content: In addition to his OMB General Counsel role, in 2025 Paoletta served as Acting Chief Legal Officer of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau [Finding #11191]. On April 16, 2025 he issued a staff memorandum announcing a CFPB shift away from federal supervision and enforcement toward a states-led model [Finding #11191]. On April 18, 2025 he signed a declaration filed in the US District Court for the District of Columbia describing the agency's "particularized assessment" of CFPB employees designated for reduction in force; Judge Amy Berman Jackson questioned the declaration's accuracy in proceedings that produced a preliminary injunction in favor of the National Treasury Employees Union [Finding #11191]. The CFPB sequence demonstrates that Paoletta's Trump-II legal work extends beyond OMB regulatory review into the operational restructuring of independent agencies. In December 2025 he was additionally designated Administrator of the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs, the OMB component responsible for centralized review of executive-branch rulemaking [Finding #11179].

sections.title: Private-Practice Lobbying and Movement Funding
sections.content: Lobbying-disclosure records show Paoletta is registered as a lobbyist at Dickstein Shapiro LLP, DLA Piper LLP, and Schaerr Jaffe LLP across his private-practice years [Finding #7068]. In 2021 he lobbied for Oracle America on federal contracting through Schaerr Jaffe, with disclosures listing OMB General Counsel and Counsel to the Vice President among his covered positions; according to LDA registration data and OMB-coordination records, Oracle paid Schaerr Jaffe at least mid-five-figure lobbying fees on government-contracting matters before Paoletta returned to OMB to coordinate with DOGE [Finding #7120][Finding #7157]. According to OGE Form 278 disclosures filed prior to his 2017 entry into government, Paoletta reported approximately $387,000 in DLA Piper income, $209,000 in MP Strategies income, and Judicial Education Project consulting income [Finding #6691]. FEC records show he donated $26,575 to Republican causes between 2022 and 2024, with the largest single tranche to Republican Party committees and an employer field listing Schaerr Jaffe LLP [Finding #6690][Finding #7073]. He is a director of Unreported Story Society (EIN 82-3412341), a 501(c)(3) conservative-media nonprofit, and is mentioned in PSQ Holdings Inc. (NYSE: PSQH) 8-K disclosures dated August 20, 2025 [Finding #7071][Finding #7084]. OpenSanctions designates him a Politically Exposed Person in two datasets [Finding #7092].

sections.title: Schaerr Jaffe and the Federalist Society Network
sections.content: Schaerr Jaffe LLP, where Paoletta was a partner from March 26, 2021 through January 2025, is a Washington litigation boutique whose partner roster has a disproportionate Federalist Society and conservative-cause representation profile [Finding #11197]. Records of the firm list partners Gene C. Schaerr (founding, seven Supreme Court arguments), Erik S. Jaffe, H. Christopher Bartolomucci, Donald M. Falk, Jeffrey W. Munk, Brian J. Field, Edward H. Trent, and Paoletta; senior counsel Charles Burnett and Nicholas Miller; counsel Hannah Smith (formerly of Becket Fund), James Heilpern, Stephanie Freudenberg, and Joshua Prince; and academic affiliates Thomas R. Lee, Eugene Volokh, James C. Phillips, John Greil, and Annika Boone Barkdull [Finding #11197]. Representative-client disclosures include Hobby Lobby, the United States Conference of Catholic Bishops, EWTN, Bayer A.G., Suzuki Motor, AT&T, Fox Corporation, the Cato Institute, the US Chamber of Commerce, the Hatch and Lee senate offices, the Republic of Ecuador, and the US Virgin Islands [Finding #11197]. The firm filed a Trump v. United States (No. 23-939) amicus brief on behalf of Edwin Meese III on March 19, 2024 with Schaerr as counsel of record, and former associate Stephen Schwartz was confirmed to the US Court of Federal Claims [Finding #11197]. Schaerr Jaffe also became a frequent litigation venue for Elon Musk and X Corp. while Paoletta was a partner; analysis of corporate and government records indicates that this representation overlapped temporally with his subsequent return to OMB as legal counsel for DOGE operations [Finding #6693][Finding #7129].

sections.title: Systemic Position and Cross-Network Bridge
sections.content: Cross-reference of corporate registry, lobbying disclosure, FEC, court, and primary-source records indicates that Paoletta is a single node simultaneously seated in five movement institutions: the Center for Renewing America (Vought / Project 2025), OMB executive-power architecture (impoundment memoranda, the funding-pause memorandum, CFPB restructuring, and DOGE coordination), the Thomas household (counsel to Ginni Thomas, the Created Equal book, the justicethomas.com and anitahillcase.com domains), the Leonard Leo / Federalist Society judicial pipeline (confirmation preparation for Gorsuch, Kavanaugh, and Thomas), and the Schaerr Jaffe DC litigation boutique [Finding #11201]. Network analysis of the broader investigation database places Paoletta at the top of the orchestrator-score ranking with a score of 39.02 on a three-pillar breadth covering government, legal, and consulting roles, derived from twenty-eight findings, fifteen connections, and three core entities [Finding #11167]. Cross-reference of the Round-6 corrections record indicates the functional pattern is parallel to but structurally distinct from the three-instance Skadden-to-Office-of-the-Comptroller-of-the-Currency revolving-door involving Adam J. Cohen, Brian Brooks, and Jonathan Gould; Paoletta was not at Skadden and was not at OCC, but examination of the vault-firm-to-OMB pattern (Schaerr Jaffe to OMB General Counsel through both Trump terms) shows the same structural mechanism reproduced in a different agency cluster [Finding #11201]. Examination of the sequence of Trump-II legal artifacts (impoundment memorandum, M-25-13, CFPB priority-shift memorandum, OIRA designation) indicates that Paoletta's output is best characterized as durable scaffolding for executive-power and deregulatory positions rather than as a series of ad-hoc opinions [Finding #11187][Finding #11191][Finding #11201].

sections.title: Relevance to the Epstein Investigation
sections.content: Paoletta's connection to the broader Epstein investigation profile is structural rather than direct: he sits in the Federalist Society / Thomas household / Trump executive-power orbit that overlaps with several other figures under investigation. According to cross-reference of investigation records, his private representation of Ginni Thomas, his preparation of Justices Gorsuch, Kavanaugh, and Thomas for confirmation, and his concurrent OMB and CFPB roles in 2025 place him in the same legal-architect tier as Adam J Cohen, where examination of the parallel revolving-door pattern documented in this investigation indicates structural equivalence [Finding #11193][Finding #11201]. LittleSis records a social relationship between Paoletta and Peter B Rutledge, a US district judge for the Southern District of Georgia [Finding #7089]. Examination of court dockets indicates open questions about whether his OMB legal work has produced opinions that would come before Justice Thomas on the Supreme Court without recusal [Finding #7054][Finding #7059][Finding #7087].
